key_terms.sense: attributing a found stain to another woman rather than to oneself
key_terms.definition: The lenient principle in stain law that lets a woman who finds a blood stain attribute it to another person or source who is equally or more likely to have caused it, so that she herself need not be deemed impure.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The daf repeatedly asks how much the borrower must stand to lose, and how plausible a source of bleeding she must be, before the lender may attribute her stain to her.

key_terms.sense: having a presumptive status of one who menstruates
key_terms.definition: A woman is classified as "seeing" if she has already experienced a menstrual flow, or as merely "fit to see" if she is old enough to menstruate but has not yet done so; only such women can serve as plausible sources to whom a stain may be attributed.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Rav limits attribution to a gentile who has already seen blood; Rav Sheshet and Rava rework the baraitot to show the dispute is really between one who has seen and one merely fit to see.

key_terms.sense: a lesser zava observing a clean day against a day of discharge
key_terms.definition: A woman who saw a single day of unusual discharge (a minor zavah) must count one clean day free of discharge before immersing and becoming pure; if she sees discharge again on that day, she must restart.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The Gemara asks whether a lender may attribute her stain to such a woman on her second day, when doing so would cost her a day of counting, versus her first day, when it costs her nothing.

key_terms.sense: attributing a new stain to a woman already impure only from a prior stain
key_terms.definition: The question whether one may attribute a newly found blood stain to another woman whose own impurity likewise derives only from a previously found stain, rather than from an actual known flow of blood.
key_terms.on_this_daf: R. Yochanan asks R. Yehuda bar Livai this question according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel; the answer, and a contradictory baraita, are resolved through several reinterpretations culminating in Ravina's rereading.

key_terms.sense: an object not susceptible to ritual impurity, applied to stain law
key_terms.definition: R. Nechemia's principle that a blood stain found on an object incapable of contracting ritual impurity (such as stone, the ground, or the outside of an earthenware vessel) does not render the woman impure, since stain law is built within the structure of impurity transmitted via objects.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The Gemara grounds R. Nechemia's ruling in a verse, extends it to the outside of earthenware vessels and to small rags, and defends it as normative halacha against an incident where the Sages ruled strictly.
aliases: kol davar she'eino mekabel tum'ah eino mekabel ketamim

key_terms.sense: the timing after intercourse that determines a woman's retroactive impurity
key_terms.definition: Bar Padda's division of the time after intercourse into three stages -- the interval in which bleeding could begin, the interval needed to rise and wash, and any longer interval -- used to fix whether a woman was impure during intercourse (obligating a chatat), only doubtfully so (asham talui), or not at all (exempt), and correspondingly whether items she touched beforehand are impure, suspended, or pure.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Rav rules that the other two sleepers may rely on a check only within this first period, following bar Padda's linkage of the husband's offering to the status of her taharot, which R. Oshaya then disputes.

key_terms.sense: mutual attribution among several women sharing a bed
key_terms.definition: Where several women sleeping together find blood beneath one of them and none can be singled out by examination, the rule by which a woman in a state exempting her from expected bleeding (pregnant, nursing, old, or not yet of age) may attribute the blood to a companion who is in her normal bleeding years.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The baraita spells out the pairs (pregnant/not pregnant, nursing/not nursing, old/not old, pre-menstrual/post-menstrual) by which the women attribute the blood to each other, and rules that if both share the same exempting state, all are deemed fit to see and all are impure.
